why: Taiwan's population and household-income figures are open data, but they come as tables, and nobody reads thirty years of tables for fun. The atlas plays them on a map instead. It began at a 2017 Chiayi hackathon; the 2026 rewrite dropped a green-to-red scale that red-green colour-blind readers couldn't tell apart.
gains: Anyone wondering whether a county grows from births or from people moving in can watch it month by month since 1997, with that month's news beside the map, and send the exact view as a link instead of a screenshot of a spreadsheet.

lessons: The 2017 JSON held up: of 20,082 overlapping population numbers only 5 differed, each by 0.01 from source corrections, and all 1,890 household figures matched.
Government tables write '-' for zero, and the data backs it: in 39 of the 40 months where natural increase is '-', total growth equals social growth.
Download links can't be hard-coded: the household-survey files change path every year, so each fetch looks them up on data.gov.tw first.
subtitle: Three decades of Taiwan, on a map
description: Play through population change across Taiwan’s 22 counties, compare their trends and explore household income. A 2017 hackathon project, rebuilt in 2026.
longDescription: An interactive atlas of population and household finances across Taiwan. Monthly population data starts in 1997, with annual income and savings indicators alongside it. A playback timeline, county comparison charts and shareable URLs turn the original 2017 Chiayi hackathon project into a tool for exploring change.
features: Population, migration, income and savings indicators
Animated timeline with adjustable playback speed
Compare trends across up to four counties
Government open data with reproducible conversion scripts
